title: Modern LaTeX Editions of Public-Domain Mathematics Manuscripts
description:
This record is the public front page for an ongoing open project to produce modern, inspectable LaTeX editions and translations of older mathematics and physics manuscripts. Public-domain scans and source/reference materials are collected, transcribed into TeX, checked into readable PDFs, organized by author/work or coherent corpus, and published with source artifacts so readers can inspect, correct, fork, and continue the work.

GitHub mirror: Forkable reader PDFs, source TeX where practical, and current manifests are mirrored at https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts. Zenodo remains the archival DOI surface and large-file/provenance backstop.

Current project map.

  • Main corpus and bulk preservation record: [##########] 100/100 this landing record remains the broad cumulative surface, with reader PDFs, artifact ZIPs, manifests, and full-repository preservation material. Latest version: this Zenodo record page; concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20393488; earlier broad cumulative record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410262.
  • EGA working English translation and source package: [###-------] substantial working translation and source package; [##########] French originals present EGA I-II are largely inherited from the community translation. Current project additions include EGA 0_IV sections 15 through 23 and EGA IV sections 1 through 21 as substantive working translations. The current record includes a broad EGA working reader, a separate 514-page EGA IV sections 1-21 working reader, all eight NUMDAM French originals as direct top-level PDFs, and TeX/source packets in ZIP artifacts. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20414353.
  • SGA working English translation: [#####-----] corpus-wide working translation; SGA 4 is the largest current compiled reader; SGA 5-7 are active partial assemblies Current SGA record with coherent cumulative readers and source artifacts. Top-level readers include SGA 1-2 English snapshots, a cleaned 1,389-page SGA 3 English rebuild, SGA 4 as a 484-page current working reader, SGA 5 as a current working draft from available segments, SGA 6 as a 231-page current working draft, and SGA 7-I current working drafts. A source-checkable SGA 5 strict restart is included separately as paired French-source and English high-fidelity readers through complete Expose V, covering scan pages 13-262 and printed pages 1-250; the next strict source point is Expose VI. French reference PDFs for SGA 1-7 remain included for checking. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410947.
  • Non-European and multilingual mathematical manuscripts: [#########-] working multilingual release with targeted layout and reader-surface repairs; broader corpus expansion continues Consolidated release for Chinese, Indian/Sanskrit, Islamic/Arabic, and historical-reference mathematical works, organized as direct work-level PDFs, source/provenance/audit ZIP artifacts, and a public guide/summary. The latest public surface contains 58 direct reader PDFs, 2,971 rendered pages, and a Brahmagupta reader-surface replacement with a compact text layer; held candidates and visually weak drafts are preserved in ZIP artifacts until rebuilt. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410957.
  • Chinese mathematical classics: [########--] 80/100 focused corpus slice for Chinese mathematical works including Jiuzhang Suanshu / Nine Chapters, Li Ye, Qin Jiushao, Sunzi, Yang Hui, and Zhu Shijie material, with language-separated readers and source artifacts. Current record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410957.
  • Indian and Sanskrit mathematical classics: [########--] 80/100 focused corpus slice for Aryabhata, Bhaskara II, Brahmagupta, and related Sanskrit/Indian mathematical works, with original-language drafts, translations, and source artifacts. Current record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410957.
  • Islamic and Arabic mathematical texts: [########--] 80/100 focused corpus slice for al-Kashi, al-Khwarizmi, al-Tusi, Omar Khayyam, Robert of Chester/Karpinski, Rosen, Ruska, and related Arabic/Islamic mathematical works, with original-language drafts, translations, and source artifacts. Current record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410957.
  • Historical reference texts for non-European mathematics: [#######---] 70/100 focused reference slice for Said al-Andalusi, al-Muqaddasi, Ibn al-Nadim, Ibn al-Qifti, Smith-Karpinski, and related contextual reference texts used for terminology and historical comparison. Current record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410957.
  • Heinrich Weber: [######----] broad draft available; literal repair stream begun author page with original-language modern LaTeX readers for Lehrbuch der Algebra Volumes I and III, plus English translation drafts. The older Volume II English reader remains available as a broad working draft, while the high-fidelity repair stream now supplies paired German/English readers for the Volume II tail and Volume III sections 1-37. TeX sources, source pages, component PDFs, rendered translation pieces, and provenance are preserved in the artifact ZIP. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20412153.
  • Emmy Noether: [#####-----] older cumulative draft retained; paper-level high-fidelity edition in progress author page with a selected mathematical-papers modern LaTeX draft, a 261-page older English translation/summary working reader, and source-checkable paper-level German/English pairs. Paper 01 has paired German/English readers; Paper 02 is complete with paired German editable and English high-fidelity readers; and the current cumulative paper-level pair runs through Paper 09 section 4. TeX, source scans, and build reports are preserved in the artifact ZIP. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20412587.
  • Deligne papers: [##########] 90/90 original-language reference PDFs preserved; [#####-----] English working translations continue dedicated Deligne record with a combined English translation-draft supplement, a grouped ZIP of the 90 original-language reference PDFs, and separate paper-level English translation supplements including Paper 32 The Weil Conjecture II through section 1.8 and Papers 42, 45, 56, 57, 58, 69, 70, 71, 83, 84, 85, 87, and 88. Individual bilingual TeX/PDF sidecars, working source layers, render checks, and provenance material are preserved in thematic artifact ZIPs. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410853.
  • Carl Friedrich Gauss: [#######---] 3,000+ pages of modern-LaTeX working drafts available; detailed proofreading continues dedicated Gauss author page with cumulative Werke band readers and source artifacts. The current local pipeline has addressed several known mathematical transcription defects and preserves source material for continued checking. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20410934.
  • Bernhard Riemann: [#######---] 70/100 author page for selected mathematical papers and a broader Gesammelte Werke complete-draft reader, with TeX/source/provenance artifacts. Current record: 10.5281/zenodo.20429778.
  • Cayley, Dedekind, and Dirichlet: classical algebra and arithmetic shelf: [#---------] Cayley front-facing repaired slices; [#########-] broader Cayley source material preserved focused shelf for modern LaTeX working drafts by Cayley, Dedekind, and Dirichlet. The current record promotes 77 repaired/retyped Cayley slice PDFs, 2,030 pages total, as direct top-level readers after a raw-TeX/process-word sweep. Broader Cayley per-volume working PDFs, TeX chunks, source trees, and audits remain in the artifact ZIP rather than being presented as clean finished readers. Dedekind Bands I-III and one Dirichlet selected-works grouping remain available as working drafts. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20414787.
  • Minkowski, Hecke, Landau, Sylvester, Steinitz, Hensel, Oka, Hausdorff, Grassmann, and Killing: [######----] 60/100 author-cluster record for cleaner reader PDFs and source/provenance artifacts. The Landau reader is the English Goodman translation of Elementary Number Theory; Sylvester collected-papers source scans for Volumes I and IV are preserved in the artifact ZIP for future modern LaTeX typesetting. All-version record: 10.5281/zenodo.20411006.

Workflow provenance. Review sessions identify and prioritize older public-domain or otherwise suitable works for transcription and translation; readers are welcome to suggest works or point to better public PDFs/scans. Local archive tooling downloads and indexes scans and source packets, prepares working folders, audits files, organizes public releases, and publishes through the Zenodo API. Large-scale machine-assisted transcription systems convert scans to TeX drafts, which are preserved as source/provenance artifacts. Review passes check, repair, and translate the TeX. Public organization is by author, work, or coherent corpus; reader-facing files use author/work/corpus titles, while provenance archives preserve source material for reconstruction.

Full repository preservation update. The current working inputs and source packets are included directly on this already-linked original/main record as ten chunked ZIP files, plus a manifest and README. There is no separate public raw-source DOI. These are provenance/backstop files for reconstruction and continuation; the reader-facing records remain organized by author or corpus.

File organization. Top-level PDFs are reader-facing files intended for browsing and direct download. ZIP files contain TeX/source material, source scans or reference material where appropriate, OCR text, provenance, manifests, audit outputs, and repair queues. Records are being split by author or coherent corpus while this main record remains the single landing page and bulk preservation surface.

Coherence note. Redundant records are being handled conservatively: cleaner author/corpus pages become the recommended public entry points, while older broad shelves are retained as preservation surfaces until their contents are fully superseded, checked, and linked. This avoids losing work while making the front-facing archive progressively easier to browse.

Quality note. These are working scholarly drafts, not final critical editions. Technical PDF audits check whether files open and extract text; they do not prove mathematical correctness. Some drafts still need layout repair, source comparison, theorem-number checking, and human proofreading. Availability is preserved while cleaner organized versions are built.
